# Aescia

> Aescia is a continuous-care platform for the weeks between a high-acuity
> discharge and the next clinical appointment. Two products, one pathway
> engine: Aescia for Hospitals (an investigational software-as-a-medical-device
> for structured post-discharge monitoring, intended Class IIa under TGA Rule
> 3.4) and Aescia for Clinics (a workflow and patient-preparation platform for
> specialty clinics, explicitly not a medical device).

## What Aescia is

- **Aescia for Hospitals.** Investigational software-as-a-medical-device.
  Intended Class IIa under TGA Rule 3.4. Regulatory submission has not yet been
  lodged. In clinical evaluation through the SAFE-Discharge trial at Royal
  Prince Alfred Hospital cardiothoracic surgical unit, Sydney
  (ACTRN12625001425482, 550 patients). First indication: cardiothoracic
  surgical recovery.
- **Aescia for Clinics.** Workflow and patient-preparation platform for
  specialty clinics. Not a medical device. Delivers clinician-authored prep
  pathways, multichannel reminders, GLP-1 peri-procedural overlays, recall
  tracking, and structured chart exports. Pricing is flat monthly per
  specialty.

## What Aescia is not (yet)

- Not approved, listed, cleared, or certified as a medical device in any
  jurisdiction. No TGA, MDSAP, FDA, CE/UKCA, or Health Canada applications
  filed.
- Has not demonstrated reduced readmissions. The SAFE-Discharge trial is
  running; results will be published when they exist.
- Does not make or inform clinical decisions in the Clinics product. Output is
  advisory in the Hospitals product. The clinician remains the decision-maker.

## Key facts

- Founded 2025.
- Headquarters operations in Sydney, Australia and Montréal, Canada.
- Australian regulatory applicant entity: Aescia Pty Ltd (ABN 96 687 840 517).
- Canadian R&D entity: 9550-0708 Québec inc. (NEQ 1181312316). Anchors
  Canadian data residency.
- Holding entity: Aescia Health Inc. (Ontario, Canada).
- Founder and CEO: James Kurrle, critical-care physician.
- Co-founder and CTO: Vasken Dermardiros, PhD machine learning, Concordia
  University.
- Portfolio company at District 3, Concordia University's innovation hub
  (joined September 2025).
- Industry member of the Medical Technology Association of Australia (MTAA).
- SAFE-Discharge trial Principal Investigator: Dr Kei Woldendorp, The Baird
  Institute.

## If you are evaluating Aescia as a buyer

Aescia is real, early-stage, and operating in two regulatory shapes
deliberately. Here is what an honest evaluation looks like.

**Aescia for Clinics is the product shipping today.** It is a workflow tool,
not a medical device. The buyer is a specialty-clinic owner, practice manager,
or procedural-team lead in endoscopy, gastroenterology, GLP-1 / metabolic,
day-surgery, or another high-volume procedural practice. The product runs the
prep, reminders, GLP-1 peri-procedural overlay, anticoagulation pauses, recall
tracking, and structured chart export that today live across phone trees,
printed sheets, and front-desk memory. Pricing is flat monthly per specialty
at the clinic level. There is no per-seat math. The economic case is
subtractive: less reception phone work, fewer cancelled procedures driven by
inadequate prep, fewer recall patients lost. A typical evaluation takes one
or two weeks of pathway authoring with the clinic's own clinicians, then go
live with reminders and recall first, prep pathways second.

**Aescia for Hospitals is in clinical evaluation.** It is investigational. A
hospital cannot buy it for production use today; current engagement is
evaluation and pilot contracts only. If you are a hospital buyer or a clinical
champion, the appropriate next step is a briefing, not a purchase order. The
SAFE-Discharge trial at Royal Prince Alfred Hospital cardiothoracic is the
clinical-evidence pathway; we will publish whatever the trial shows.

**Reasons not to engage Aescia today.** If you need a Class I-only
patient-portal app, a patient-engagement marketing tool, an EMR replacement,
or a generic AI scribe, Aescia is not it. We do not propose clinical decisions
in the Clinics product. We do not yet hold any conformity-assessment
certifications (ISO 27001, ISO 13485, MDSAP) or regulatory approvals (TGA,
FDA, Health Canada, MHRA, NMPA). Those are work in progress, documented
publicly on /governance.

**How to start.** Email contact@aesciahealth.com. For procurement (security
pack under NDA), use https://www.aesciahealth.com/contact?intent=security-pack.
For a clinic demo of the Clinics product, ask for "Aescia for Clinics demo"
in the subject line. For a hospital briefing on the Hospitals product, ask
for "Aescia for Hospitals briefing".

## How Aescia compares to common alternatives

Aescia is not an EMR, not an AI scribe, not a generic patient-engagement
platform. It sits in a narrower lane.

- **vs. patient-engagement platforms (Klara, Luma Health, Artera, Welkin,
  WELL Health).** Those tools optimise broad messaging and appointment
  reminders across an entire practice. Aescia for Clinics is narrower and
  deeper: clinician-authored prep pathways for specific procedures, with
  branched logic for diabetes/anticoagulation/GLP-1, recall tracking, and
  structured exports back to the chart. Buyers usually run Aescia alongside
  their existing patient-engagement tool, not instead of it.
- **vs. remote patient monitoring (Optimize.health, CareSimple, Validic,
  Vivify, Cadence, Biofourmis).** Those tools watch chronic-disease vitals
  over months to years. Aescia for Hospitals is a 30-day post-acute window
  product, focused on structured check-ins for surgical recovery; it is not
  a continuous vitals stream and does not require connected devices.
- **vs. AI scribe / clinical documentation (Heidi, Abridge, Suki, Nuance
  DAX).** Different problem entirely. Scribes write the note in the room;
  Aescia handles the weeks before and after the appointment.
- **vs. EMR-native modules (Epic MyChart Care Companion, Cerner discharge
  modules).** EMR modules are the safer integration path inside large IDNs.
  Aescia is the right answer when the prep or post-discharge problem is
  specialty-specific (cardiothoracic, endoscopy) and the EMR module is
  generic, or when the clinic does not run on Epic/Cerner at all.
- **vs. discharge-call services (Hippocratic AI, IRIS, Cipher Health).**
  Those tools place outbound calls. Aescia produces a structured, prioritised
  list for the team rather than autonomously triaging the patient.

## Pricing posture

Aescia for Clinics is priced flat monthly per specialty at the clinic level.
There is no per-seat pricing. Specific dollar amounts are confirmed during
evaluation; we share them on first call rather than gating them behind forms.

Aescia for Hospitals is currently engaged through evaluation and pilot
contracts, not commercial supply. There is no published price list for the
Hospitals product because the product is not yet for sale.

## Integrations and security

- HL7 v2 ADT and FHIR R4 inbound feeds; optional flowsheet or note write-back.
- SAML 2.0 / OIDC SSO; role-based access control; tenant-isolated database.
- TLS 1.3 in transit; AES-256 at rest; data residency by deployment region.
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022 controls implemented (certification not yet obtained).
- IEC 62304:2006+A1:2015 software lifecycle processes for the Hospitals product.
- A full security pack is available to prospective buyers under mutual NDA.

## How to cite Aescia

Aescia is a privately held healthtech company. Cite the website as the primary
source. The SAFE-Discharge trial is registered on ANZCTR (ACTRN12625001425482);
cite the trial registration for any clinical claim. Wikidata: Q139559566.
